assessment.summary: BTK (Q06187) is an exceptionally well-validated drug target with 170 PDB structures (best resolution 1.08Å), over 21,000 ChEMBL IC50 entries, and 6 approved drugs including ibrutinib, acalabrutinib, zanubrutinib, and pirtobrutinib. The target has strong disease validation in B-cell malignancies and primary immunodeficiencies, with active ongoing research including next-generation non-covalent inhibitors and PROTACs. Druggability is unambiguously high across all evidence dimensions.
evidence_gaps: Resistance mechanisms to covalent BTK inhibitors (e.g., C481S mutation) remain an active clinical challenge, though non-covalent inhibitors like pirtobrutinib partially address this
Selectivity profiling across the full kinome for newer-generation inhibitors may be incomplete in public databases
PROTAC-based BTK degraders are still in early discovery/clinical stages — their long-term efficacy and safety profiles are not yet established
Structural data for BTK in complex with resistance mutants (e.g., C481S, T474I) may be underrepresented in public PDB entries
CNS penetration and blood-brain barrier data are limited for most approved BTK inhibitors, relevant for CNS lymphoma indications
